fact: NC State Extension lists water, urea, uric acid, lactic acid, creatinine and bilirubin as the major components of dog urine.
quote: The major components of dog urine include water, urea, uric acid, lactic acid, creatinine, and bilirubin (Chang, Huang, and Li 2018).
source_label: NC State Extension, Dogs and Turfgrass Interactions (AG-905, Grady Miller, July 21, 2021)
notes: Read in full with curl on 2026-09-25. The publication is about lawns; this record is used only for what dog urine contains.

fact: Montana State University Extension explains that the urease enzyme turns urea and water into ammonium, which then converts to ammonia gas that escapes near the surface.
quote: Volatilization depends on the rate of urea hydrolysis (see Chemical Reactions; Equation 1), and the rate at which the ammonium is then converted to ammonia gas (Equation 2) that volatilizes if near the soil surface. … urease urea + water → ammonium Equation 1: Hydrolysis increases pH ammonium → ammonia gas Equation 2: Volatilization faster at higher pH
source_label: Montana State University Extension, Factors Affecting Nitrogen Fertilizer Volatilization (EB0208, revised June 2020)
notes: Written about urea fertilizer on soil. The page uses it as the same urea chemistry, framed as research on fertilizer, never as a turf study.

fact: Montana State University Extension says warm temperatures speed the conversion of urea to ammonia gas, and that a rise from 45°F to 60°F can double the loss when moisture stays the same.
quote: Warm temperatures increase the rate of urea hydrolysis and ammonium conversion to ammonia gas, and therefore volatilization. For example, an increase in temperature from 45°F to 60°F can double volatilization loss when moisture content is kept the same (14).
source_label: Montana State University Extension, Factors Affecting Nitrogen Fertilizer Volatilization (EB0208, revised June 2020)
notes: (14) is the publication's reference number, not a figure the page uses.

fact: Montana State University Extension says cool temperatures slow the formation of ammonia but do not stop it, leaving ammonia that escapes slowly over a longer period.
quote: However, cool temperatures do not ensure reduced volatilization. Although cool temperatures decrease the rate at which ammonia is formed, they also decrease the rate that ammonium and ammonia are converted to nitrate, bound to clays, tied up (immobilized) by microorganisms, or taken up by plants. Soils also stay moist longer at low temperatures. These factors leave more ammonia in solution where it can volatilize slowly but over a longer period of time when temperatures are low.
source_label: Montana State University Extension, Factors Affecting Nitrogen Fertilizer Volatilization (EB0208, revised June 2020)

fact: Montana State University Extension says it generally takes 0.5 inch or more of precipitation in a single event to carry urea deep enough into soil to stop it turning to ammonia gas, and that losses were largest on a moist surface followed by slow drying.
quote: Largest losses in Montana (30 to 44 percent of applied N) occurred when urea was applied to a moist soil surface, followed by a period of slow drying with little or no precipitation (Figure 2). … Generally, 0.5 inch or more of precipitation from a single weather event is needed to leach urea deep enough into the soil to protect it from volatilization.
source_label: Montana State University Extension, Factors Affecting Nitrogen Fertilizer Volatilization (EB0208, revised June 2020)
notes: Field trials on cropland in Montana and Oregon. The page applies it to urine only as the same chemistry, and says so.

fact: Montana State University's urea research found that light scattered rain often is not enough moisture and may increase ammonia loss rather than prevent it.
quote: At least 0.5” rainfall in a single event is needed to move urea into the soil deep enough to minimize or prevent volatilization. Light scattered rain is often not sufficient moisture; it may increase rather than prevent volatilization losses.
source_label: Montana State University, Urea Volatilization research: What Have We Learned?

fact: The nearest NOAA station, Greeley UNC, averages 73.5 days a year with at least 0.01 inch of precipitation but only 7.8 days with 0.5 inch or more, 2.6 of them in June through August (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053553 GREELEY UNC — ANN-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE001HI 73.5 · ANN-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE050HI 7.8 · JJA-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE050HI 2.6
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, annual/seasonal, station GREELEY UNC (USC00053553)
notes: GE001HI = average days with 0.01 inch or more; GE050HI = 0.50 inch or more; JJA = June–August. Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in noaa-normals-greeley-unc — say "the nearest NOAA station".

fact: The nearest NOAA station, Longmont 2 ESE, averages 72.3 days a year with at least 0.01 inch of precipitation but only 7.8 days with 0.5 inch or more, 3.1 of them in June through August (1991–2020 normals).

source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, annual/seasonal, station LONGMONT 2 ESE (USC00055116)
notes: GE001HI = average days with 0.01 inch or more; GE050HI = 0.50 inch or more; JJA = June–August. Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in noaa-normals-longmont-2ese.

quote: USC00053005 FT COLLINS — ANN-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE001HI 85.9 · ANN-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE050HI 8.7 · JJA-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE050HI 2.6

fact: The directions for one enzyme odor product sold for artificial turf say to saturate the whole turf area and not to rinse it, so the product can air dry and keep working.
quote: Attach the bottle to your garden hose and turn on the water. Set the nozzle to the "ON" position. Thoroughly saturate the entire turf area. Do not rinse; allow the product to air dry and continue working.
source_label: CareFree Enzymes, Synthetic Turf Odor Destroyer: directions for use
notes: A manufacturer's label, cited as an example of how turf enzyme products are applied, not as an endorsement. The page does not repeat the maker's safety or effectiveness claims.

fact: One outdoor enzyme odor maker's directions call for at least 10 minutes of contact, 20 to 30 minutes for old deposits, no rinsing afterward and no contact with bleach.
quote: Allow a minimum dwell time of 10 minutes. For old deposits, extend to 20 to 30 minutes. Do not rinse. The enzymes need uninterrupted contact time to fully digest the uric acid. … Correct application - full surface saturation, minimum 10-minute dwell time, no immediate rinsing, no bleach contact - is what determines whether the result lasts.
source_label: Nature's Freedom, Enzyme Pet Odor Remover: How It Works and Why It Lasts (manufacturer's guide)
notes: Manufacturer's own guide; used for its application directions only.

fact: Consumer Reports, testing cleaners on carpet stained with real dog urine, says enzyme cleaners need longer to work and are mostly biodegradable and nontoxic, while oxidizing cleaners with hydrogen peroxide and bleach work faster but aren't safe on every surface.
quote: Enzyme cleaners require a longer dwelling time to work, but most are biodegradable and nontoxic. Oxidizing cleaners work faster on stains, but because they contain ingredients like hydrogen peroxide and bleach, they aren’t always safe for all surfaces.
source_label: Consumer Reports, enzyme and oxidizing cleaners for pet stains and odors (May 28, 2026)
notes: The test was on carpet samples stained with real dog urine, not turf. The page says so.

fact: Humane World for Animals recommends enzymatic cleaners for pet urine odors and advises against ammonia or vinegar, whose strong smells may encourage a pet to mark the same spot again.
quote: If you can still see or smell the soiling, wash again with an enzymatic cleaner—these break down pet waste odors. … Avoid cleaning chemicals such as ammonia or vinegar. Strong chemical odors may encourage your pet to reinforce the urine scent mark in that area.
source_label: Humane World for Animals, How to remove pet stains and odors
notes: Written for indoor soiling; the page applies only the re-marking point to a dog area outdoors.

fact: The U.S. Geological Survey lists odor control as the second-largest U.S. use of natural zeolite, 15% of 2025 domestic sales, with synthetic turf among its other uses.
quote: Domestic uses were, in descending order of estimated quantity, animal feed, odor control, unspecified end uses (such as ice melt, soil amendment, and synthetic turf), water purification, pet litter, wastewater treatment, oil and grease absorbent, fertilizer carrier, gas absorbent, aquaculture, desiccant, fungicide or pesticide carrier, and catalyst. Animal feed and odor control accounted for 42% and 15%, respectively, of the domestic sales tonnage.
source_label: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026: Zeolites (Natural)
notes: The sales year is 2025 (the summary's opening line: "In 2025, seven companies operated seven zeolite mines").

fact: A zeolite infill maker describes zeolite in pet turf as neutralizing ammonia from urine rather than masking the odor.
quote: One of the most effective modern uses is artificial turf infill for pets, where zeolite helps neutralize ammonia from pet urine instead of masking odors.
source_label: ZeoFill, What Is Zeolite? (manufacturer's page)
notes: A maker's description, presented on the page as what makers say, not as a test result.

fact: Greeley's municipal code prohibits an owner or keeper from allowing an animal to damage the property of another.
quote: It is prohibited for an owner or keeper to allow an animal to damage the property of another, including public property. Any finding of violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor infraction.
source_label: Greeley Municipal Code Sec. 10-64, Damage to property (Ord. No. 33, 2019; Supplement 6 Update 1)
notes: Read through the Municode API (job 493697, product 18000). The code does not say whether urine on turf counts as damage; the page hedges and says so.

fact: Greeley's municipal code requires an animal's owner or keeper to remove feces the animal leaves on someone else's property right away.
quote: The owner or keeper of an animal shall immediately remove any feces deposited by the animal upon the property of another, including public property and common areas. Any finding of violation of the section shall be a misdemeanor infraction.
source_label: Greeley Municipal Code Sec. 10-65, Animal waste removal (Ord. No. 33, 2019; Supplement 6 Update 1)
notes: Read through the Municode API. A search of the Greeley code for "urinate" found only the human public-urination section (Sec. 14-150).

fact: Milliken allows hand-watering, with a hand-held hose fitted with a positive shutoff nozzle or a bucket, every day, outside its lawn-sprinkling restrictions.
quote: Hand-watering and drip irrigation shall be permitted Monday through Sunday and not be restricted by the above-mentioned lawn-sprinkling restrictions. Hand-watering shall mean holding in the hand a hose with an attached positive shutoff nozzle or a bucket and does not include operating a hose with a sprinkler or manually operating an irrigation controller.
source_label: Town of Milliken, Watering Schedule
notes: Same page as milliken-watering-schedule (sprinkler hours). The page does not name artificial turf.

fact: Severance makes it unlawful to use any outside water source between 11 a.m. and 5 p.m., and allows hand watering of flowers, shrubs and trees each day during permitted hours with a shut-off hose.
quote: No watering shall be allowed between 11:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. Hand watering of flowers, shrubs, and trees shall be allowed each day by hose during permitted hours, provided such hose has a shut-off valve attached which terminates flow when not manually activated. It is unlawful to use any outside water sources between 11:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M.
source_label: Town of Severance, Watering Guidelines and Restrictions
notes: Standing rule, not a 2026 drought stage (see severance-mandatory-schedule). The page does not name artificial turf.

fact: Johnstown's Level 3 FAQ bars watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., asks that hand watering be done on the property's scheduled day with an automatic shutoff nozzle, and says hardscapes should not be spray-washed.
quote: Under Level 3, the Level 2 standards restrictions and exemptions still apply, with the addition that the property's designated watering day are reduced to 2 times a week. These restrictions are in place from April 20 to October 15, 2026. Watering between the hours of 10 a.m. - 6 p.m., is NOT permitted at any time. … Hardscapes (driveways, sidewalks, patios, etc.) should not be spray-washed. Use dry-cleaning methods such as sweeping or spot cleaning when possible. … Hand watering and supplemental irrigation for items such as vegetable gardens, decorative pots, hanging baskets, and similar plantings should be done on-site and in a water-efficient manner on the properties' scheduled watering day with an automatic shutoff nozzle to prevent water waste.
source_label: Town of Johnstown, Water FAQs: Water Conservation Level 3
notes: Johnstown's Faq.aspx?QID=239 to 241 links redirect to this category page. The FAQ does not name artificial turf.

fact: After Johnstown's outdoor watering season ends on October 15, its 2026 schedule allows hand watering of trees and shrubs on Saturdays and Sundays.
quote: October 15 is the end of outdoor watering season. After October 15, you may hand water trees and shrubs on Saturdays and Sundays.
source_label: Town of Johnstown, 2026 Watering Schedule
notes: The schedule names trees and shrubs only; it does not say whether rinsing artificial turf is allowed after the season ends.
